recommendation: Keep the empty audit. If the work group wants existing no-valueSet example bindings migrated to descriptive, handle that as follow-up to FHIR-48325 or a new terminology decision rather than as a DSTU1 FHIR-8704 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-8704 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core profiles issue asking that unbound bindings, meaning bindings without a valueSet reference, not publish a required binding strength; the Jira example was Encounter.hospitalization.reAdmission.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commits 8f49b5a5d1b3c665726162148b67a86bef8bc9f6, aba5a84eb72c0b924c56a0a719df63525e6137c7, and 5277cd48bd7e1b226a0190a07c1e4d728b245ce3. Those commits first suppressed strength for BindingMethod.Unbound, fixed null rendering, then settled on BindingStrength.EXAMPLE for unbound bindings because ElementDefinition.binding.strength was required in that model.
additional_context: Encounter.hospitalization has since been renamed to Encounter.admission; the current active Encounter source gives Encounter.admission.reAdmission an example strength and the v2-0092 valueSet. Later FHIR-48325 added the descriptive binding strength and invariant for descriptive bindings without a valueSet and is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-46606 removed the obsolete terminologies Unbound section, and current terminologies source has no such section.
reconciliation: No source change was made. A current scan of StructureDefinition XML found 17 binding elements with strength and no valueSet, all with strength example and none required, extensible, or preferred, so the seed defect is not present in current source.

related_jiras.note: Added descriptive binding strength and the descriptive-without-valueSet invariant for R6; already represented on the combined branch, so this worker did not duplicate it.
Removed the obsolete terminologies Unbound section; used only as background confirming later vocabulary policy moved away from that old prose.
